body.text: The design provides defense in depth through prevention, detection, containment, suppression, and safe shutdown.
body.anchor: takes into account prevention, detection, containment, suppression, and the ability to maintain safe shutdown

body.text: Requirements consider both conventional and sodium fires.
body.anchor: for both conventional and sodium fires

body.text: The sodium fire strategy uses leak prevention, detection, and passive mitigation.
body.anchor: utilizes leak prevention, detection and passive mitigation

body.text: The radiological sodium strategy uses passive features, and adds active features only where necessary.
body.anchor: only add active features (e.g., inert gas flooding systems) where necessary

cells: Rooms with limited leak rate and known oxygen volume, inerted or de facto inerted
rows.anchor: Cells are rooms with a limited leak rate and known oxygen volume

cells: Full secondary pressure boundary for radiological sodium
rows.anchor: Guard pipes act as a full secondary pressure boundary

cells: Like guard pipes, but with a drainpipe to a collection location

cells: Guard enclosures placed where pipe inspections are needed

body.text: Clamshells in the HAA drain leaked IHT sodium to the RAB pipe chase, so a leak inside is not a leak into the HAA.
body.anchor: a leak from the piping within the clamshell is not a leak into the HAA

body.text: Suppression decks are used on catch pans where oxygen volume cannot be limited.
body.anchor: Suppression decks are applied to catch pans where the environmental oxygen volume cannot be limited

body.text: Conventional fire detection in non-inerted fire areas gives supplemental leak detection.
body.anchor: Conventional fire detection installed in non-inerted fire areas provides supplemental sodium leak detection

checks.q: What is the difference between a guard pipe and a guard enclosure?
o: A guard enclosure has a drainpipe
checks.x: Guard enclosures act similarly, except that a drainpipe is attached.

checks.q: Where does a clamshell in the HAA drain?
checks.x: Clamshells allow leaked sodium to flow to the RAB pipe chase.

o: Where oxygen volume cannot be limited

cells: Contained or drained, with sloped floors and steel plates to a catch pan

cells: Evaluated against the Quantitative Health Objectives

body.text: Leaked radiological sodium stays within the process cell. Non-radiological sodium may drain to lower catch pans or vaults.
body.anchor: Leaked radiological sodium is contained within the process cell

body.text: Detection of small leaks helps prevent large leaks.
body.anchor: Detection of small leaks helps prevent large leaks from occurring

checks.x: Drain lines are heat traced to minimize sodium freezing.
checks.anchor: are heat traced, where needed, to minimize sodium freezing

checks.q: Where does leaked radiological sodium stay?
checks.x: It is contained within the process cell.
checks.anchor: Leaked radiological sodium is contained within the process cell

body.text: Leaks are postulated for all piping that normally contains sodium.
body.anchor: Leaks are postulated for all piping that normally contain sodium

body.text: Design basis leakage cracks are Dt/4 for seismic piping, and full circumferential breaks for non-seismic piping.
body.anchor: a Dt/4 crack for seismically qualified piping and a full-circumferential break for non-seismically qualified piping

body.text: Sodium and salt systems are evaluated as moderate energy systems.
body.anchor: Liquid sodium containing systems are evaluated as moderate energy systems

body.text: SSCs in the HAA are protected from the worst-case leak regardless of stress.
body.anchor: SSCs in the HAA are protected from the worst-case leak, regardless of stress

body.text: A top of pipe spray could make a faster, hotter fire. A bottom leak could make a larger volume flood.
body.anchor: could create a faster, hotter fire that directly impacts some SSCs

checks.q: What leak size is postulated for seismically qualified piping?
checks.x: It is bounded by a Dt/4 crack.
checks.anchor: a Dt/4 crack for seismically qualified piping and a full-circumferential break for non-seismically qualified piping

o: Sodium and salt leaks can have more significant effects
checks.x: Leaks in smaller pipes are considered due to potentially more significant environmental effects.
checks.anchor: Due to the potentially more significant environmental effects of sodium and salt leaks

body.text: Redundant trains of safety-significant and safe shutdown SSCs are in separate fire areas.
body.anchor: Redundant trains of Safety-Significant and safe shutdown SSCs are located in separate fire areas

body.text: Damage from any single fire is limited to a single fire area.
body.anchor: Damage caused by any single fire is limited to a single fire area

body.text: The design limits fire damage to a single train.

body.text: Fire analyses and fire PRA will be done for the operating license application.

checks.q: What does the design assume about equipment in a fire area?
checks.x: A safe shutdown path is kept while assuming all equipment in any one fire area is rendered inoperable.

body.text: There is no active or manual fire suppression for large sodium fires.
body.anchor: There is no active or manual fire suppression for large sodium fires

body.text: Sodium leaks and fires are mitigated passively by NNA features.
body.anchor: Sodium leaks and resulting sodium fires are mitigated by passive means

body.text: Class D extinguishers with Sodium Chloride-based dry powder are staged for personnel protection.
body.anchor: Class D fire extinguishers containing Sodium Chloride-based dry powder

body.text: Incipient conventional fires in the RAB and RXB use Class A, B, or C extinguishers.
body.anchor: manual firefighting methods using Class A, B, or C fire extinguishers are used

body.text: Beyond the incipient stage, offsite responders with specialized training are requested.
body.anchor: offsite responders with specialized training are requested to respond

body.text: Deep-seated sodium fires are contained in NNA features and are passively self-suppressing.
body.anchor: are passively self-suppressing

body.text: The RXB and RAB have no water-based suppression, to avoid sodium-water interaction.
body.anchor: do not contain water-based fire suppression systems to avoid sodium-water interaction

body.text: A Fire Protection Program will be developed at the OL stage to meet 10 CFR 50.48(a).
body.anchor: A Fire Protection Program for operations will be developed at the operating license stage

checks.anchor: do not contain water-based fire suppression systems to avoid sodium-water interaction

title: Fire Protection and Sodium Leakage
subject: fire protection
intro: Sodium fires change the fire protection picture. Passive features do the work, and water stays away from sodium. This lesson pairs with SY-15.

objectives.text: State the fire protection defense-in-depth approach for conventional and sodium fires.
Describe the sodium leak design features.
Explain how each category of sodium leak is handled.
Describe how leak sizes and locations are postulated.
Explain the fire safe shutdown strategy.
State the preliminary firefighting strategies and the role of operators and responders.
